findings.summary: 'Count your tool calls against the order below' gives the planner nothing to count against
findings.evidence: The rule tells the planner to count its tool calls against a reading order. The order is a sequence of steps (deliverables, then callers, tests and config, then the rest), not a number. Decision 3 rejects a call limit because no per-run data exists. So 'count' has no threshold, and the only thing the planner can act on is the stopping condition ('once every criterion has a demonstration and a seam, write the plan'). This is an estimate from reading the rule text, not a measurement. Fix: Change the wording to 'follow the order below; you cannot see the time', or say plainly that the order and the stopping condition are the measure. Do not imply a count the planner can check. Keep the test needle `You have no clock of your own`.

findings.summary: At the live 86400 s value the stated figures say almost nothing, so the change mostly helps short configured deadlines
findings.evidence: athena.toml:224 sets `planner_timeout_s = 86400`, since commit 740a9e4 (HISTORY.txt:90). The brief would say 'stop exploring by 43200 seconds'. The plan admits this, and the CHANGELOG entry and the doc comment will say so. The parts that help at any deadline are the fixed text ('sends no plan') and the order-based stopping condition. Fix: No change to the plan is needed. In the changelog, put the order-based stopping condition first and the figure second, so a reader does not expect a measurable effect at the live value.

findings.summary: The stop-path assertions only guard existing behavior, and the double supplies the reason text
findings.evidence: The wrapper sets `turn.detail = Some(format!("deadline of {n}s reached"))`. The asserted reason then passes through planning.rs:190-198 unchanged, so the assertion confirms the production path forwards the detail; it does not check the text itself. The plan already labels this part a guard (Decision 7). Fix: No change needed. Optionally, also assert `verification_passed == None` (planning.rs:13) to pin the rest of the stop path.

summary: I read the code and checked the plan's claims against it. They hold. `PlannerInputs` (planner.rs:33) and `planner_brief` (planner.rs:95) exist, and neither carries a deadline. The only production literal is in `planning_round` (planning.rs:129), and it reads the same `cfg` whose `planner_timeout_s` goes to `agent_spec` (planning.rs:162). The only test literal is the `planner_inputs` helper (briefs.rs:2788). The Report size pin (briefs.rs:3963-4004) and the `split("## Report")` tests are not affected, because the new section sits before `## Report`. No test pins the planner brief's full heading list. The run-test helpers all exist as cited: `athena_with`, `repo_with_config`, `planning_script`, `prompts_of`, `finished_job` and `timing_out`. `stop_planning` (planning.rs:8-14) fails the job with `PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX`. Each demonstration would fail without the change: the unit test uses two deadlines in both rounds, and the run test uses two configured values (600 and 4321) and compares the brief figure with `spec.timeout`. The plan states honestly that the live deadline is now 86400 s because of commit 740a9e4 (HISTORY.txt:90), and that the rule is prose, not enforcement. The dependents list covers the CHANGELOG readers in `refusal_corpus` and the budget test. The plan follows the accepted reading and the request's preference for giving the stage information over a refusal rule, so I found no soundness problem at blocker or major level. What remains is minor: the reading order gives the planner no count to compare its tool calls against, and the change does little while the live value is 86400.
